scope: Current React/V1 bounded transport, explicit owned pending-command recovery, and complete mocked table browser regression. Not full M04/M06, hosted, provider or capacity acceptance.
sourceState: Uncommitted urgent-repair working tree; preserve unrelated owner and agent changes.

behavior.transport: One default 15000 ms deadline spans fetch and response.json consumption. Deadline aborts the request and settles even if body consumption ignores abort. Caller AbortSignal and reason are retained.
behavior.ambiguity: Timeout or lost response does not establish server rejection or rollback. Retain the original command ID and validated request fields until an owned receipt or definite rejection resolves it.
behavior.storage: Separate session/review pending entries are tab, owner and game scoped. Only validated request metadata/action fields are stored. Control lease capability is omitted; a SHA-256 lease fingerprint permits exact reconstruction from a freshly fetched matching token. No private history, review frames, advice or analysis is persisted.
behavior.expiry: Stored entries expire 24 hours after creation and are discarded on read after expiry, malformed content or owner mismatch. Logout attempts and HTTP 401 erase pending entries. In-memory fallback remains available if browser storage rejects writes.
behavior.recovery: No automatic replay on reload. Ownership checks use GET /api/identity and generated IdentityView {playerId}, which does not load/project the active game. Positive owner change clears rendered and referenced current session, pending identity and generation-fences old responses, including ApiFailure.current. Mutations are blocked until a fresh owned session is loaded. Accepted live commands use owned status-only reconciliation followed by the current SessionView. Initial anonymous opening calls the existing create-capable GET /api/session before the no-create identity read. Pending restore waits for verified ownership. If the active view fails but identity succeeds, an owned durable receipt remains available for explicit reconciliation. Unknown-owner reconnect continues through same-command receipt recovery rather than hiding an unresolved pending request.
behavior.review: A queued or interrupted trial retains commandId, trialId, decisionId, alternative and expectedRevision. Explicit retry first retrieves an already-ready owned result; otherwise it retries the identical original request. Different alternative creation is blocked while unresolved.
behavior.visualScope: No stylesheet or table geometry changes. App.tsx only wires ReviewPanel onOwnerChanged to controller.invalidateOwner; review uses existing retry-button styling.

findings: Preparation publication requires the exact computing attempt ID and expires_at > clock_timestamp(); a rejected or expired earlier claimant cannot publish over a newer attempt. The wall clock check runs at publication after lock acquisition.
Starting access generation, current owner/session, active game, coverage, control lease, revision, observation and policy are rechecked before publication/commit.
Issued preparation receipts are retained independently while jobs remains the current game/revision pointer.
Owned command status and ready review result reads use loadGame:false; these routes do not calculate or grant new gameplay.

Ownership verification now uses GET /api/identity with loadGame:false; receipt recovery is independent of a quarantined active-state account projection. See service.json for executed server identity evidence.

limits: Browser checks intercept API routes and prove client behavior, not deployment or end-to-end PostgreSQL composition.
Browser persistence can be unavailable; while that tab lives, the fallback retains the in-memory request. Reload durability requires successful browser storage.
No full repository suite, Go port, provider, hosted capacity, strategy-quality, native or human-learning acceptance was run by this agent.
